insights.insight: $4.75M in cryptographically verified purchase receipts across 89,628+ transactions establishes a proof-of-purchase dataset at a scale where category and brand-level targeting signals become statistically meaningful — not a pilot, a running ledger.

Each receipt in this protocol is a confirmed purchase event, not an inferred intent signal — the same distinction that separates a loyalty card swipe from a cookie-based lookalike audience, but with cryptographic attestation rather than retailer goodwill.

The 7-day window has closed above $94K on ten of twelve consecutive days, with six closings above $101K and a new high of $103.4K on Oct 12 — the floor is rising, not holding flat, which indicates organic receipt submission growth rather than a static panel.

The 14-day brand mix spans mass (Walmart, 349 receipts), club (Costco, 132), conventional grocery (Kroger, 160; Safeway, 125), home improvement (Home Depot, 60), and QSR — meaning purchase signals cross channel types, which is the cross-retailer view that no single loyalty program can provide.

insights.topic: Stable payout economics signal real user incentive
insights.insight: The protocol has maintained a roughly stable dollar-equivalent payout per receipt by adjusting sats/receipt inversely with BTC price — 765 confirmed payouts with 14.8M sats claimed suggests the incentive structure is functioning and not cannibalizing data quality through spam submissions.

Twelve consecutive UTC midnight rollovers show post-rollover GMV floors rising from the low $80Ks to $88.5K, providing a clean, repeatable baseline cadence that brand measurement teams could use to isolate lift windows without relying on panel-based control groups.
